question: Does the public Taft River fish abstract provide fish names that can be safely admitted as waterbody-specific species records?

waterbody.name: Taft River and Taft River Basin
waterbody.administrativeArea: Taft, Eastern Samar; the wider basin and Bagacay mining-source area also involve Hinabangan, Samar
waterbody.identityContext: Keep the Taft River study's Eastern Samar downstream setting distinct from the Bagacay mine-source area in Hinabangan, Samar, and from other Samar rivers with similar regional labels.
waterbody.geometryDecision: No boundary or sampling geometry added. The reviewed fish abstract only says three river sections; it gives no section coordinates or reach names.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Morallos, S. A., Ultra, V. U., Jr., Cabahug, M. R. S., Celeste, N., Espejon, E. J., Jr., Tan, Z. N., & Bejar, F. R. (2025). Impact of Bagacay Mines on Heavy Metals Accumulation and Associated Health Risk of Fishes from Taft River, Philippines. EM-16-07, 16th International Conference on Environmental and Rural Development Book of Abstracts, p. 61.
sourcesReviewed.access: Publisher-hosted 223-page abstract book opened and the EM-16-07 entry visually/textually inspected at PDF page 97, printed page 61. The full underlying fish study, sample-level data, and species-by-reach table were not located.

reportedResults.reportedArea: three sections of Taft River; section names and fish-to-section allocation are not given

sourcesReviewed.decision: Retain the nine exact source strings as research leads only. No taxonomic normalization, per-reach occurrence, freshwater-only classification, current presence, local diet, catchability, or public-app projection is approved.
limits: The abstract does not state field dates, gear, effort, named stations, coordinates, salinity, tidal context, fish-to-section allocation, vouchers, or identification diagnostics.
The phrase ‘three sections’ does not establish that all sampled reaches are freshwater rather than brackish or estuarine; retain habitat salinity as unresolved.

The abstract reports health-risk calculations but provides no underlying fish-by-site measurements or full methods. They are not a current fish-consumption advisory and do not establish conditions outside the sampled material and study assumptions.

No item-specific license or derivative-data reuse permission was found for the abstract book. Keep the taxon list out of public app data pending fuller source, identification, site, and rights review.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Sabijon, J., Ultra, V., Jr., Bollido, M., Espejon, E., Jr., & Tan, Z. N. (2025). Heavy Metal Contamination in Taft River Sediments Affected by Bagacay Mine Post-Operation in Hinabangan, Samar, Philippines. Environment and Natural Resources Journal, 23(5), 390-408. https://doi.org/10.32526/ennrj/23/20250026
sourcesReviewed.access: Publisher article page and abstract reviewed. It concerns river-bank and river-bottom sediments, not fish or biotic samples, and recommends expanding monitoring to biotic components.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Use only as separate, dated sediment-study context for the basin. It does not validate the fish abstract's species identifications, fish-tissue results, or a present-day human-health advisory.
sourcesReviewed.license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International stated on the publisher article page; this review retains citation and factual notes only.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Science Council of Asia. (2021). 21st Science Council of Asia Conference programme of activities. Poster presentation listing: Impact of Bagacay Mines on Heavy Metals Accumulation and Associated Health Risk of Fishes from Taft River, Philippines, by Shian A. Morallos.
sourcesReviewed.access: Official conference-program PDF search result reviewed; it lists a poster with the same title and presenter as the 2025 abstract, but contains no fish names, methods, or results.
sourcesReviewed.decision: Treat as a possible earlier communication of the same research, not independent fish evidence. The program alone does not prove that the 2021 poster and 2025 abstract used the same specimens or dataset.

crossSourceAssessment.versionRelationship: The 2021 conference program and 2025 conference abstract share the poster title and presenter; they may represent repeated communication of one research project. No evidence establishes independent surveys or a sample-level link, so do not count them as two datasets.
crossSourceAssessment.regionalContext: The 2025 sediment article describes a contaminated sediment basin and calls for biotic monitoring. Sediment and fish studies are different evidence lanes; neither substitutes for current official food-safety monitoring.
crossSourceAssessment.taxonomy: The nine fish names are preserved as printed strings only. Accepted-name status, authority, diagnostics, and specimen identifications were not cross-checked in this pass.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Source discovery lead only. No complete, voucher-linked or site-by-taxon fish inventory, current occupancy, legal/catchability guidance, species-level diet, fish-safety conclusion, or publishable data license was established.

disposition.reason: A conference abstract supplies nine source-name leads but lacks the site, habitat, identification, sampling, voucher and reuse details needed to publish structured species records.

nextActions: Continue the Samar Island Natural Park river sweep by searching inspectable, rights-clear studies for river-by-species tables and methods; do not send inquiries without explicit authorization.

Seek the full fish study or author-approved dataset for the Taft River abstract, including field dates, reach names/coordinates, salinity or tidal context, gear/effort, specimen vouchers, fish-by-site contaminant results, analytical methods, and dataset reuse terms.
Keep any consumption-risk evidence separate from fish occurrence and require a current, competent public-health or environmental authority before publishing a safety advisory.
Audit the remaining Eastern Visayas provinces and inland waters before marking Region VIII complete; this single abstract does not complete Eastern Samar or the region.

sources.supports: EM-16-07 abstract, printed page 61: nine fish names, three river sections, and abstract-level fish-tissue/consumption-risk results.
2025 Taft River Basin sediment study scope, findings, stated biotic-monitoring limitation, and CC BY-NC 4.0 article-page license.
2021 Science Council of Asia program listing the same poster title and presenter; no species results.
